camera: Hasselblad EDC, Zeiss Biogon 5.6/60, calibrated focal length 61.1 mm, reseau plate 10 mm grid
alsj_caption: 135:01:56 Frame from Ed's Station H pan. Rightward of 9486 (9486: 'Photo toward the LM from Station H. We are looking ESE. Al is to the left of the spacecraft... aiming the TV camera at the MESA.')
alsj_source: ALSJ Apollo 14 Image Library (hq.nasa.gov/alsj/a14/images14.html, via web.archive.org)

camera_height_m.note: chest-mounted Hasselblad on standing suited astronaut

digitization_process: Every coordinate below was read manually from labeled-grid crops of the full-resolution scan rendered by digitize_helper.py (grid steps 10-50 px, coordinates in full-image pixels, origin top-left, x right, y down). Sigmas are 1-sigma reading uncertainties judged per feature (fuzzier penumbrae and rock/shadow boundaries get larger sigmas). This is an up-sun photograph: rocks present their shaded faces to the camera and partially occlude the near end of their own shadows, so 'base' points are placed on the visible shadow-band axis near the casting object rather than at an exact (occluded) ground contact, and carry correspondingly larger sigmas.
